name: The Grove at Pinewood
headline: Ulysses Development Group plans The Grove at Pinewood, a 49-unit, four-story family apartment building for households at 40-60% AMI on vacant land beside its 103-unit Pinewood Lodge senior property at 200 S. Ironton Street in Aurora; it won $1.8 million a year in federal 9% credit, $500,000 in state credit and $98,000 in TOC credit in CHFA's 2026 Round One.
why_it_matters: It is an infill second phase on surplus land at an existing affordable senior property, using an Aurora Housing Authority special limited partnership to get a tax exemption and to offset Aurora's high water, sewer and impact fees; the AHA board took up that partnership in August 2026.

status.label: Credits awarded; housing authority partnership in progress; closing not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA lists the award as of 2026-09-30. The Aurora Housing Authority board agenda for 2026-08-13 lists a special limited partnership presentation for The Grove at Pinewood and action on AHA Board Resolution No. 688; No public source shows the outcome. The applicant said it could close within six months of an award and break ground by the end of 2026; There is no public closing, permit or groundbreaking record.

next_step: Get the Aurora Housing Authority minutes for 2026-08-13 to confirm whether Resolution No. 688 (the special limited partnership) passed, then watch City of Aurora records for the minor subdivision plat and building permits.

key_numbers.meaning: 17 one-bedroom, 16 two-bedroom, 16 three-bedroom family apartments at 40-60% AMI (average 56.33%).
About $18M over the 10-year credit period, plus $500,000 state credit and $98,000 TOC credit.
The applicant commits to the 15-year compliance period plus a 25-year extended use period.
The same 49 units applied as Pinewood Modular in 2025 Round One and were not funded.

background.text: Ulysses acquired Pinewood Lodge, the existing 103-unit affordable senior property on the same parcel, in May 2024, per its 2025 narrative; the Grove is the second of two phases meant to create a cross-generational campus with shared parking, outdoor amenities and a shared management agreement. The purchase price is not public.

The same 49-unit design (17/16/16 bedrooms; 36 at 60%, 8 at 50%, 5 at 40% AMI) applied in CHFA's 2025 Round One as Pinewood Modular, requesting $1,598,467 federal 9%, $650,000 state and $63,700 TOC credit; it is not on the 2025 Round One award report.

Land and local deal: about 1.57 acres will be split off from the 4.57-acre parcel through a City of Aurora Minor Subdivision Plat. Since November 2024 Ulysses has proposed an Aurora Housing Authority special limited partnership that would give the project the authority's waitlist and tax-exempt status and help offset Aurora's water, sewer and impact fees; AHA sent support letters, and further SLP steps were to follow an award.

The Aurora Housing Authority board scheduled a special limited partnership presentation for The Grove at Pinewood, an executive session on real estate matters, and action on AHA Board Resolution No. 688 at its 2026-08-13 meeting.

Community outreach, per the applicant: a first public meeting in January 2025 (noticed to Pinewood Lodge residents and in the Sentinel) and a second meeting with Lodge residents in December 2025; Lodge residents raised concerns about construction and added density.
Environmental: the Phase I ESA found no recognized environmental conditions; radon is a business environmental risk, and a passive radon mitigation system is planned, per the applicant.

Applicant says the project meets Enterprise Green Communities and DOE Zero Energy Ready Homes standards and is consistent with the Aurora Places Plan's call for family and senior housing in diverse neighborhoods.

discrepancies.text: The 2025 narrative says the Prop 123 Concessionary Debt predevelopment award was up to $489,500, while the 2026 narrative says Ulysses received $538,230 in May 2025.
The 2025 narrative puts the project on about 1.14 acres of a 4.5-acre parcel, while the 2026 narrative says about 1.57 acres of a 4.57-acre parcel.
Ulysses's 2025 narrative says Pinewood Lodge serves residents at 50% to 60% AMI, while another applicant's 2026 Round One narrative lists Pinewood Lodge as 55+ at 40-60% AMI.
